tasks.short: Reproduce and analyse usability issues, discuss them with developers, write issue tickets, and follow up the fixes.

steps.what: Web administrator analyses usability issues and reproduces them
Web administrator collaborates with development teams to discuss and resolve usability issues
Web administrator writes issue tickets with steps and screenshots
Web administrator follows up fixes with developers by chat

tasks.design: Tickets for developers ({PROJECT}) are created from the service desk ({HELPDESK}) with the page, browser and screenshot already attached, and status changes notify the administrator instead of chasing by chat. Reproducing issues and agreeing fixes with developers stay with the administrator. Gathering user feedback is a separate task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tickets were written from scratch and fixes chased by chat.
tasks.enabler_now: Service desks pass context into developer tickets and send status updates.
tasks.still_hard: Vague complaints still need a call to the user.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which complaint points to a design flaw rather than a bug.

evidence.claim: Service desks can create developer tickets with context attached and notify on status changes.
Screenshots from users can contain personal data and are kept only as long as needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from the usability issue to the fix followed up; gathering feedback and building the fix are outside.
Input contract: service desk linked to the developers' ticket tool; fallback is writing tickets by hand.
Developers update ticket status as before.

incremental.description: Web administrator keeps the ticket link between the tools working.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few issues per month; high: many issues passed to developers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan user tests and recruit users, run test sessions, note and type up observations, and decide findings and recommendations.

steps.what: Web administrator plans user tests and recruits test users by e-mail
Web administrator performs user testing to determine the site's usability
Web administrator notes observations during sessions and types them up afterwards
Web administrator decides findings and recommendations on the site's effectiveness

tasks.design: Test users sign up through a panel form and book a session slot themselves ({CALENDAR}), so recruiting is not arranged by e-mail. Sessions are recorded with consent in a testing tool ({OTHER}) where the administrator tags moments during the session, so observations are linked to the recording instead of typed up afterwards. Running sessions and deciding findings stay with the administrator. Routine usage tracking is a separate task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Users were recruited by e-mail and notes typed up after each session.
tasks.enabler_now: Testing tools record sessions with timestamped tags; booking pages take sign-ups.
tasks.still_hard: Some user groups are hard to recruit online.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing where a user hesitates without saying so.

reach.learn: Whether booking a session is easy.

evidence.claim: User testing tools can record sessions and link timestamped tags to the recording.
Recording test users processes personal data and needs their consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test needed to findings decided; redesign is outside.
Input contract: test users consent to recording; fallback is handwritten notes.
Test users book in about the time an e-mail took.
research_questions: Are findings ready sooner after testing?

incremental.description: Web administrator keeps the test panel current.
Test users book their own session.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few in-person tests with hard-to-reach users; high: regular remote tests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect change details from tickets and deploy logs, write change descriptions, update change procedures, check the documentation, and publish it to the team wiki.

steps.what: Web administrator collects change details from tickets, commits and deploy logs
Web administrator documents application and web site changes in the change log

loop.input: The merge request description, its linked tickets and the list of changed files.
loop.output: A draft change log entry in the team's format.
loop.check: Every listed change must map to a commit or ticket in the merge request, or it is dropped; the administrator edits every entry.
loop.stop: One draft per merge request; if rejected, the administrator writes the entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Commit messages alone are too terse for readers outside the team.

steps.what: Web administrator updates change procedures when steps change
Web administrator checks the final change log and procedures
Web administrator publishes the documentation to the team wiki and notifies the team

tasks.design: For changes that go through the deployment pipeline with linked tickets, about 80%, the change record is built from the merge request, tickets and deploy time ({OTHER}), so details are not collected by hand; emergency fixes are still documented by hand. A bounded step drafts the change log entry; changes that do not map to a commit or ticket are dropped and the administrator edits every entry. Procedure documents show the pipeline configuration changes beside them, so the administrator updates only affected steps. Once checked, the documentation is published to the team wiki ({DOCS}), which notifies the team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change details were gathered from several tools and written up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Pipelines record what was deployed; language models draft entries that can be checked against commits.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a change note that operators can act on at night.
tasks.altitude: The administrator edits change notes instead of writing them.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for review.
Language models can draft change notes that can be checked against commits and tickets.

assumptions: Boundary: from the change deployed to documentation published; making the change is outside.
Input contract: merge requests linked to tickets; fallback is writing by hand.
Scenario: about 80% of changes go through the pipeline with linked tickets.
The administrator checks every entry before publishing.
research_questions: How much of each drafted entry is kept?

already_counted.description: Web administrator edits drafted change log entries.

incremental.description: Web administrator keeps the change log template current.

approvals.approved_version: The change log and procedures as checked by the administrator in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many emergency fixes outside the pipeline; high: nearly all changes through the pipeline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Export usage data into spreadsheets, compile the monthly usage report, analyse trends, check the report, and send it to stakeholders.

steps.what: Web administrator tracks web site usage data by exporting it into spreadsheets
Web administrator compiles the monthly usage report
Web administrator scans the monthly views for drops and spikes beyond the set thresholds
Web administrator analyses usage trends and the causes of anomalies
Web administrator checks the final usage report
Web administrator e-mails the usage report to stakeholders

tasks.design: A usage dashboard ({BI}) connected to the analytics tool holds the standard monthly views, so data are not exported into spreadsheets, and the monthly report is generated from it with space for the administrator's comments. Fixed rules flag drops or spikes beyond set thresholds, so the administrator starts the analysis from the flags. Once checked, the report goes to stakeholders from the dashboard. Analysing trends stays with the administrator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Usage data were exported and charted by hand each month.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards connect to analytics tools and send scheduled reports.
tasks.still_hard: Consent banners leave gaps in the data.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why traffic dropped after a redesign.
tasks.altitude: The administrator analyses instead of compiling.

evidence.claim: Dashboards can connect to web analytics tools and send scheduled reports.
Analytics cookies that track visitors need consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the month ended to the report sent; site changes are outside.
Input contract: analytics connected to the dashboard; fallback is exports.
The administrator checks every report before it goes out.

incremental.description: Web administrator maintains dashboard views and thresholds.

approvals.approved_version: The usage report as checked by the administrator in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many ad hoc analyses; high: mostly standard monthly reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The web administrator keeps reproducing issues, testing with users, deciding findings and analysing trends; collected complaints, typed notes, hand-written change logs and exported spreadsheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An administrator with more time on usability.
